release_read.basis: Revenue $232.9M against a ~$198M high-end consensus (+17%) and the company's own ~$175-190M run-rate, colocation +60% q/q to $215.4M, 485 MW billing (>$700M annualised) and adj. EBITDA margin 57% vs 25%: a clear beat on the line the stock trades on, discounted because the last 13% beat was met flat, the release says nothing on Texas permits or CoreWeave and gives no numeric guide, and liquidity fell to $1.74B.

release.released_at_note: 8-K exhibit 99.1 dated 2026-11-05, before the 08:30 ET call; the release states no time of day
release.headline: Core Scientific reports Q3 2026 results: revenue $232.9M, colocation revenue $215.4M (+~60% q/q), 485 MW billing, adj. EBITDA $133.6M (57% margin)

vs_bar.note: consensus disputed in the hunt: $169.7M-$198.4M across sources; against the low end the beat is ~35%
driven by a non-cash warrant fair-value gain (net income $1,178.1M); not comparable. Nasdaq fallback forecast $0 (2 estimates)
against the hunt's run-rate of ~$159M/quarter at 437 MW (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001839341/000183934126000013/q22026corescientificinc-ea.htm)

key_line.detail: 485 MW billing at 2026-09-30 (395 MW at Q2), over $700M average annualised colocation GAAP revenue; first colocation agreement nearing full delivery, second under construction across five campuses. No mention of Texas permits or CoreWeave by name; a new $295.0M deferred lease incentive on the balance sheet is unexplained; liquidity + DSRA fell to $1.74B from $2.60B.

guidance.detail: No numeric Q4 or 2027 guide; only 'substantial contracted capacity still to deliver'. The street had no company guide either.

call.detail: Call held at 08:30 ET; no transcript or coverage of its content found by 09:20. Whether it answered the Texas permit question is unknown to this review.

public_reaction.summary: No analyst actions, call coverage or retail tone found in the time available.

tape_read.note: Robust reference 12.80 vs prev close 12.76 (+0.3%), 67 prints, 11 in the last 30 min, last 09:13, not stale. The pre-market ran to 13.60 (+6.6%) and sagged back to flat (low 12.50) while the call was on, with QQQ -1.1%. Against a +5% release read and a 9.7% implied move the price holds almost none of the beat; the sag suggests the call or the tape (Nasdaq weak, AI-infra credit) did not add support.

thesis_check.note: The thesis was a reassuring call on Texas permits into a building short; the release beats clearly on revenue and MW but is silent on Texas and CoreWeave, and the pre-market fade after the call is not the squeeze the thesis expected.

expected.open_lag_note: The pre-market move is near zero (+0.3%), so 'less than half' is close to a coin flip and there is no gap to fade; an active pre-market (not stale) that already touched +6.6% shows buyers for the beat, but the sag through the call and a -1.1% QQQ keep it balanced.

recommendation.limit_basis: About +4.2% vs prev close: inside today's pre-market range (high 13.60), roughly the release read less a discount and under half the 9.7% implied move; a bmo beat that has not been priced can reprice in the session, and the pre-market already traded there once.
recommendation.reason: De cijfers zijn duidelijk beter dan verwacht (omzet ongeveer 17% boven de raming), maar de koers staat voor de opening vrijwel vlak nadat hij eerst tot 13,60 opliep. Leg een verkooplimiet op 13,30: haalt de koers dat vandaag, dan nemen we de winst; zo niet, dan gaat de positie aan het slot weg, omdat een ochtendcijfer vaak de hele dag doorwerkt.
recommendation.what_would_change_it: Zakt de voorbeurskoers voor 09:30 onder 12,50 (het voorbeurslaagste) of komt er nieuws dat het gesprek negatief was over Texas of CoreWeave, verkoop dan op de opening.
